request.question: Why can SAP alone not answer the three epic questions?

answer:
**SAP alone cannot answer the three epic questions because it holds financial and transactional records but lacks the operational telemetry—tonnes moved, equipment health signals, and production throughput—needed to calculate unit economics, predict failures, or model operational impact.**

| Epic | What SAP has | What SAP lacks | Why it matters |
|------|--------------|----------------|----------------|
| **E1: Where the margin went** | Cost postings | Tonnes mined, processed, shipped | Cannot calculate **C1 cost per tonne** or margin without denominator *(MIXED provenance)* |
| **E2: Fix trucks before failure** | Failure notifications (after the fact) | Fleet telemetry, health signals | Warning signs appear in real-time data streams SAP does not capture; cannot **predict** 14-day failure risk *(MIXED provenance)* |
| **E3: One supplier, whole fleet** | Suppliers, stock levels | Truck-part dependencies, haulage tonnes, berth throughput | Cannot trace which of **40 trucks** (29 autonomous, 11 manned) depend on a part or model **lost shipment tonnes** if Port Hedland loader stops *(MIXED provenance)* |

**Next step:** Link SAP materials and notifications to OPS fleet asset IDs so the verified queries can join cost postings to truck telemetry, enabling per-asset margin and risk calculations across all **55 fleet assets**.

---

**Sources:**  
*MIXED:* FOB revenue Q1 FY2027 (USD 509.3 M), EBITDA Q1 FY2027 (USD 373.1 M, C1 USD 21.09/t), ore shipped FY2026 (18.21 Mt), all three epics  
*OPS:* Haul trucks (40), fleet assets (55), ore processed FY2026 (19.06 Mt)  
*SAP:* Plants 1710, 1010, 3010; workforce (1,698 people)

*This data is simulated.*
